docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-4-codex.md:11573:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:14:**M1 — `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` missing on `FormatIdWire`.** Verified empirically: `{"kind":"builtin","id":14,"extra":1}` deserializes silently to `Builtin { id: 14 }`. `qbook_format.rs:561, 571` already uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on `FormatEntry` / `FormatOverlayEntry` for exactly this protection. `NamedTargetWire` (wire.rs:137-139) lacks it too — likely a pre-existing gap rather than a step-2-introduced regression — but `FormatIdWire` going on the wire in step 4 makes the gap newly load-bearing. Either add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on `FormatIdWire` now, or document the decision (alongside `NamedTargetWire`) that wire types accept extra fields for forward-compat. Per the global "No Fallbacks" rule, silent acceptance of unknown fields is the kind of soft failure that masks producer bugs.

Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-4-codex.md:14005:Detail: This line scans `FormatTable::iter()` and returns the first matching string, but step 4 made duplicate strings legal across peer custom namespaces and across Builtin/Custom. If local peer A has replayed `Custom(B,0) = "yyyy-mm-dd"`, runtime `intern_format("yyyy-mm-dd")` returns B’s id and emits no `RegisterFormat`, while `FormatTable::intern` would allocate `Custom(A,0)`. After the LibreOffice `Custom(LEGACY,0) = "General"` case, this can also bypass builtin-first precedence because `HashMap` iteration is unordered.
docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-4-codex.md:14010:Detail: Step 4 makes arbitrary `FormatIdWire::Custom { counter: u32 }` reachable through op replay. Registering `Custom(local_peer, u32::MAX)` makes `counter + 1` overflow in debug builds and wrap to `0` in release; `set_local_peer` has the same pattern at [format.rs:310](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:310), and `intern` can also overflow at [format.rs:347](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:347). Release wrap can later overwrite or reuse lower counters.

docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-3-opus.md:14:- `to_legacy_u32(Builtin(200))` returns `Some(200)`, then `legacy_from_u32(200)` returns `Custom(LEGACY_PEER, 36)`. **The "round-trip" is asymmetric**: the storage→u32→storage hop is NOT identity for `Builtin(n)` with n≥164. The `legacy_round_trip_through_helpers` test only validates u32→storage→u32 (the safe direction).
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-3-opus.md:15:- Mitigations are environmental: production code never constructs `Builtin(n)` with n>163 (verified by grep); xlsx import / qbook loader / replay go through `legacy_from_u32` which routes 164+ to Custom. So this is contractual debt, not a live bug, but it can bite in step 4 when an in-memory FormatId crosses the wire boundary and serializes via `to_legacy_u32`.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-3-opus.md:16:- Fix this cycle by either: (a) adding a `debug_assert!(n <= FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX)` in a `Builtin` constructor and switching test sites to `legacy_from_u32(200)`; or (b) documenting the invariant prominently and renaming the test value to ≤163. Recommend (a).
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-3-opus.md:26:**L3 — `from_u32_legacy` numerical alignment is implicit.** Both crates compute the boundary with different identifiers (`FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID = 164` in storage; `FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX + 1` in wire). They agree today (164) but no single source of truth links them. A `const _: () = assert!(...)` static check across crates isn't currently possible, but a doc-comment cross-reference exists in `FormatId::legacy_from_u32`. Acceptable but worth noting in step-8 megaudit.

docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1791:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-codex.md:11400:  `intern_format` predicts `next_custom_id` before logging (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:51`). Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. Wire impact: `RegisterFormat.id`, `SetCellFormat.id`, `FormatId(pub u32)`, and persisted qbook/xlsx mapping need a schema bump or compatibility layer.

docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:1:# Opus audit — Phase 5.2 D-1 step 2 (FormatIdWire) 2026-05-19
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:4:HEAD audited: `135bbb99f75` (Phase 5.2 D-1 step 2 — introduce FormatIdWire).
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:14:**M1 — `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` missing on `FormatIdWire`.** Verified empirically: `{"kind":"builtin","id":14,"extra":1}` deserializes silently to `Builtin { id: 14 }`. `qbook_format.rs:561, 571` already uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on `FormatEntry` / `FormatOverlayEntry` for exactly this protection. `NamedTargetWire` (wire.rs:137-139) lacks it too — likely a pre-existing gap rather than a step-2-introduced regression — but `FormatIdWire` going on the wire in step 4 makes the gap newly load-bearing. Either add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on `FormatIdWire` now, or document the decision (alongside `NamedTargetWire`) that wire types accept extra fields for forward-compat. Per the global "No Fallbacks" rule, silent acceptance of unknown fields is the kind of soft failure that masks producer bugs.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:24:**L3 — No `#[non_exhaustive]` on `FormatIdWire`.** wire.rs:281. Comparison: `WireDecodeError` (wire.rs:45) has it; `CellWireValue` + `NamedTargetWire` don't. Since `FormatIdWire` is a wire format under an already-bumped schema (Phase 5.2 D-1), and the no-fallbacks rule says future variants should produce a `WireDecodeError::UnknownFormatIdKind` rather than silently dispatching, `#[non_exhaustive]` would document the open-set intent. Low priority; deferring is fine.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:31:- `from_u32_legacy` boundary `FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX = 163` (wire.rs:295) + `+1 = 164` matches `ql_storage::FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID = 164` (format.rs:29) exactly. Round-trips through both directions: pre-5.2 save of `id=164` → `Custom { peer: LEGACY_PEER, counter: 0 }`.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:32:- No pre-5.2 reserved sentinel ids exist that need rejection — `FormatId(0)` = General is a legitimate builtin; all other `0..=163` are Excel canonical or sparse-unregistered. No special-case needed in `from_u32_legacy`.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:34:- No arithmetic on `Op::RegisterFormat.id: u32` or `Op::SetCellFormat.id: Option<u32>` in replay (replay.rs:497-540) or producer (formats.rs:41-114) — only `==` / `lookup` lookups + `>= FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID` filter at save (qbook_format.rs:1179). Step 4 swap is a clean signature change at these sites; step 5 reads the filter through `from_u32_legacy`.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:36:- Re-export at `ql_oplog::FormatIdWire` (lib.rs:48) is wired correctly.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:45:The wire type ships correctly, the serde shape is exactly what the spec promises, the `from_u32_legacy` boundary aligns with the existing `FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID = 164`, collision-freedom holds at the type level, and 4233 tests + the 9 new ones are clean. Step 3 can proceed.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:47:The M1 `deny_unknown_fields` gap is worth fixing this cycle (single-line annotation) because step 4 puts `FormatIdWire` on the wire and silent acceptance of extra fields is exactly the soft failure the global no-fallbacks rule forbids. M2 (test name) is a one-line cosmetic fix. L1-L4 are deferrable to step 3 / step 4 / step 5 closures as their consumers materialize.

docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-codex.md:11400:  `intern_format` predicts `next_custom_id` before logging (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:51`). Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. Wire impact: `RegisterFormat.id`, `SetCellFormat.id`, `FormatId(pub u32)`, and persisted qbook/xlsx mapping need a schema bump or compatibility layer.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-codex.md:11418:  `intern_format` predicts `next_custom_id` before logging (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:51`). Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:8828:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1791:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-codex.md:11400:  `intern_format` predicts `next_custom_id` before logging (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:51`). Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. Wire impact: `RegisterFormat.id`, `SetCellFormat.id`, `FormatId(pub u32)`, and persisted qbook/xlsx mapping need a schema bump or compatibility layer.

Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:9964:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:5708:[HIGH] `PeerId` has no serde representation for `FormatIdWire`
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:9965:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:5710:Detail: Step 2 plans a serde round-trip-tested `FormatIdWire` with `Custom(PeerId, u32)`. Current `PeerId` derives only copy/hash/order traits, so a normally-derived `Serialize`/`Deserialize` on `FormatIdWire` will fail unless step 2 adds manual serde or first gives `PeerId` a deliberate wire shape. This is also the right moment to decide whether peer ids serialize as raw `u64` or 16-hex strings.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:9966:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:5720:Detail: The checklist says “Pick one in step 1,” and step 2 already calls for `FormatIdWire::from_u32_legacy(n)`. Deferring because there is no current use site is understandable, but it creates a likely duplicate/inline sentinel in step 2.

docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14077:[MEDIUM] `FormatIdWire` silently accepts unknown fields inside variants  
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14079:Detail: The serialized shape is correct, but the enum lacks `deny_unknown_fields`. A payload like `{"kind":"builtin","id":14,"counter":7}` will be accepted with `counter` ignored, which weakens the schema-version discipline for this new wire type. `Op` itself denies unknown fields, but that does not protect nested `FormatIdWire` variant payloads.  
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14089:PASS on `from_u32_legacy`. Storage’s actual boundary is `FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID = 164` in [format.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:29). `u32::MAX` maps without overflow to `Custom { peer: LEGACY_PEER, counter: 4294967131 }`; I’d add that exact boundary test, but I don’t see a correctness bug. TOML/serde will reject negative literals for old `u32` fields before this helper runs.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14095:PASS on step-4 readiness with one caution: migration is mechanical at `Op::RegisterFormat { id: u32 }` and `SetCellFormat { id: Option<u32> }`, plus replay/runtime sites. The producer must stop relying on a global numeric `next_custom_id()` and allocate under the local peer.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14099:PASS on const placement. Keep `FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX` private here; step 5 should call `from_u32_legacy`, not duplicate `163`. A public xlsx boundary constant belongs with storage/xlsx mapping, not `ql_oplog::wire`.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14101:PASS on `Hash`. `PeerId` derives `Hash`, so `FormatIdWire`’s derived `Hash` is fine.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14108:[MEDIUM] `FormatIdWire` silently accepts unknown fields inside variants  
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14110:Detail: The serialized shape is correct, but the enum lacks `deny_unknown_fields`. A payload like `{"kind":"builtin","id":14,"counter":7}` will be accepted with `counter` ignored, which weakens the schema-version discipline for this new wire type. `Op` itself denies unknown fields, but that does not protect nested `FormatIdWire` variant payloads.  
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14120:PASS on `from_u32_legacy`. Storage’s actual boundary is `FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID = 164` in [format.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:29). `u32::MAX` maps without overflow to `Custom { peer: LEGACY_PEER, counter: 4294967131 }`; I’d add that exact boundary test, but I don’t see a correctness bug. TOML/serde will reject negative literals for old `u32` fields before this helper runs.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14126:PASS on step-4 readiness with one caution: migration is mechanical at `Op::RegisterFormat { id: u32 }` and `SetCellFormat { id: Option<u32> }`, plus replay/runtime sites. The producer must stop relying on a global numeric `next_custom_id()` and allocate under the local peer.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14130:PASS on const placement. Keep `FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX` private here; step 5 should call `from_u32_legacy`, not duplicate `163`. A public xlsx boundary constant belongs with storage/xlsx mapping, not `ql_oplog::wire`.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:14132:PASS on `Hash`. `PeerId` derives `Hash`, so `FormatIdWire`’s derived `Hash` is fine.

docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-3-consolidated.md:47:- The enum has no type-level guard preventing `FormatId::Builtin(200)`. Tests at format.rs:502+555 (pre-closure) actively used `Builtin(200)`. Consequences: `to_legacy_u32(Builtin(200))` returns `Some(200)`, but `legacy_from_u32(200)` returns `Custom(LEGACY_PEER, 36)`. The round-trip is ASYMMETRIC in the storage→u32→storage direction for misused Builtin values.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-3-consolidated.md:48:- **Closure (this commit):** (a) Strong docstring on `FormatId` documenting the 0..=163 invariant explicitly with "Callers MUST use `legacy_from_u32`" guidance. (b) Both test sites switched from `Builtin(200)` to `legacy_from_u32(200)` (= `Custom(LEGACY_PEER, 36)`), reflecting the semantically-correct mapping.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-3-consolidated.md:61:- **Closure (this commit):** accept Codex's defer recommendation. The expect()s are documented as load-bearing; step 4 will drop the Op-path expect()s by changing Op to FormatIdWire. Step 5 will drop the qbook-envelope expect()s. Step 6 will drop the xlsx-export expect()s.

docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-opus.md:33:- **Forward-readiness for step 2 is clean.** `crates/ql-oplog/src/wire.rs` (281 LOC) follows a consistent pattern: `pub enum WireDecodeError` (thiserror), `pub enum CellWireValue` (serde derive + impl), `pub enum NamedTargetWire` (serde derive + impl), plus two free helpers. Adding `pub enum FormatIdWire { Builtin(u32), Custom([u8; 8], u32) }` or `Custom(PeerId, u32)` slots in alongside `CellWireValue`/`NamedTargetWire` with no naming clash. `WireDecodeError` is `#[non_exhaustive]` (line 45) so step 2 can add a `FormatIdDecode { ... }` variant without breaking callers. `PeerId` is now accessible in-crate as `crate::PeerId` for the wire type's owned form — no re-route needed. The pub-use line in `ql-oplog/src/lib.rs:50` (`pub use wire::{CellWireValue, NamedTargetWire, WireDecodeError};`) needs a tiny extension to add `FormatIdWire` — trivial.

Codex's findings arrived later than the shell-exit notification suggested — the retry transcript at `docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md` ends with a clean triage + verdict `NOT SHIP-READY` (against the pre-W5-150 scope). codex
**Findings**

HIGH: Legacy no-header `oplog.bin` compatibility is incomplete for pre-D-1 format ops. The legacy branch only calls `OpLog::import_bytes` on the raw Loro bytes ([oplog_persistence.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io/src/oplog_persistence.rs:242)), and `import_bytes` validates Loro framing but not each JSON op ([log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:311)). Current `Op::RegisterFormat` / `SetCellFormat` require tagged `FormatIdWire` ([op.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/op.rs:122), [op.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/op.rs:146)), while old pre-step-4 raw oplogs used bare `u32` ids. A real old raw Loro `oplog.bin` with format ops can therefore load as a Loro doc but fail later on `iter()`/replay with `OpLogError::Deserialize`. If the intended compat window is only step-6 raw files, document that explicitly; otherwise add a legacy op-shape migration/normalization path.

MEDIUM: Backward-compat coverage is synthetic. The legacy test writes current `oplog.export_bytes()` and uses only value/formula ops ([oplog_persistence.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io/src/oplog_persistence.rs:269), [oplog_persistence.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io/src/oplog_persistence.rs:552)). I found no checked-in `.qbook` / `oplog.bin` fixture. Add at least one pre-header fixture with format ops, ideally one from immediately before step 7 and one from before step 4.

MEDIUM: External docs/API comments still imply raw Loro bytes are suitable as `.qbook/oplog.bin`. Most notably `CollabSession::export_bytes` says “OR for `.qbook/oplog.bin` persistence” ([session.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/session.rs:248)), and the architecture doc says `.qbook/oplog.bin` remains the same Loro snapshot blob ([crdt-data-model.md](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/crdt-data-model.md:437)). Post-D3, only `ql_io::save_workbook_with_oplog` writes the QLOL wrapper.

LOW: Header version `0` is accepted. The loader rejects only `version > OPLOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` ([oplog_persistence.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io/src/oplog_persistence.rs:232)), but only version `1` is defined. A malformed `QLOL + 0 + valid Loro body` loads as supported. Add a min-version check or reject `0`.

**Validated**

No Loro magic collision found: Loro 1.12.0 uses lowercase `b"loro"` as its blob magic, not `b"QLOL"` ([encoding.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/encoding.rs:155)). Empty bytes do error: the ignored defensive probe returned `Loro(DecodeError("Invalid import data"))`. Recovery/atomic-save code only moves directories and does not parse `oplog.bin`.

Focused checks run:
`cargo test -p ql-io tier_d3_ -- --nocapture` passed 5/5.
`cargo test -p ql-oplog --test p412_defensive_oplog_probes import_zero_length -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` passed and confirmed the empty import error.
